sense: a written message sent to someone

terms.gloss: a letter, a written message sent to someone
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.8: quās plūribus epistulīs accēpī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Any letter; in church the reading from the letters of the apostles. The Vulgate spells it epistola.

terms.gloss: a letter (one or more): the plural of littera
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 3.3.65: litterās resignāre, to open a letter (Lewis & Short s.v. littera)
terms.comment: In the plural litterae is “a letter”; the singular littera is a letter of the alphabet. So ūnae litterae, one letter; bīnae litterae, two letters.

terms.gloss: the Apostle: Paul’s letters, the epistle reading
terms.comment: In the Fathers “the apostle” is Paul, and his letters; the Orthodox still call the book of the Epistles and its reading “the Apostle”.

phrases.latin: ō suāvīs epistulās tuās ūnō tempore mihi datās duās!
phrases.english: two lovely letters of yours, delivered to me at once!
for a letter does not blush

phrases.latin: Et cum lēcta fuerit apud vōs epistola haec, facite ut et in Lāodicēnsium ecclēsiā legātur
phrases.english: And when this letter has been read among you, see that it is read in the church of the Laodiceans too

phrases.latin: ibi enim posueram cōdicem apostolī cum inde surrēxeram. arripuī, aperuī, et lēgī in silentiō
phrases.english: for I had left the book of the Apostle there when I got up. I snatched it up, opened it, and read in silence
